output.reason: Two days of black tarry stools with lightheadedness on standing suggests ongoing upper GI bleeding with possible volume loss, requiring immediate emergency assessment, labs, IV access and endoscopy capability that messaging cannot provide.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. Black, tarry stools usually mean bleeding in your digestive tract, and feeling lightheaded when standing suggests you may have lost a meaningful amount of blood. Have someone drive you rather than driving yourself; call 911 if you faint, vomit blood, become confused, or feel your heart racing. Don't eat or drink on the way.
differential: Upper GI bleed (e.g. peptic ulcer, gastritis, varices)
Small bowel or right-colonic bleeding source

citations.claim: Black tarry stool (melena) indicates GI bleeding, most often from an upper GI source.
citations.limitation: Compiled ED synthesis; melena can rarely reflect ingestion of iron or bismuth.
